findings.area: Exchange rate used to restate renminbi fees
findings.finding: The repository restates renminbi fees in dollars at 7.129 (the IRS 2025 yearly average) or 7.10. The six bank boards read today sell dollars at 6.684-6.702. Dollar equivalents of renminbi fees are therefore understated by about 6-7%: HSBC's ¥620 cap is shown as USD 86.97 and is USD 92.95 at today's reference mid; the ¥220 minimum is shown as USD 30.86 and is USD 32.98.

findings.area: 'No published spread' and modelled spread bands
findings.finding: Older sections (ladder, repatriate, briefing, verify-d5d1f860) leave the exchange-rate margin blank or model a band of 0.3%-1.5%. One section published the same morning, final-f6327e23, measures it from the Bank of China board alone and reads the same figures as this section (665.71 / 668.51 at 17:39:58, 0.21% over the bank's own mid) — an independent match. This section adds four more mainland boards and HSBC: 0.21%-0.26% for the five mainland banks and 0.50% for HSBC. The modelled band starts above what the mainland boards show.

findings.area: Fee tables rest on one bank
findings.finding: Every fee in the other cost tables comes from HSBC China's tariff. Bank of China, Agricultural Bank and China Merchants Bank publish personal wire fees on their own sites; Agricultural Bank's cap (¥200 + ¥80) is less than half HSBC's (¥500 + ¥120). Outside this section the only citation of a mainland bank's site is the Bank of China rate board in final-f6327e23; no other section cites a mainland bank's fee table.

Re-read against the tariff effective 31 October 2026: issuance 0.1% (min ¥100, max ¥500) plus ¥120 cable for Premier and Advance; free for Private Banking individuals; Global Transfer free for Private Banking and Premier, USD 20 for Advance. The repository's figures agree.

Re-read: ATM cap ¥100,000 a year and ¥10,000 per card per day; cash carrying USD 5,000 / 10,000; renminbi notes ¥20,000; annual quota USD 50,000; reconversion memo valid 24 months, USD 500 a day on ID alone; fine bands 30% and 30%-100%. The repository's figures agree.

Re-read: section 988(e) USD 200 threshold; IRS yearly averages (2025: 7.129); FBAR penalty table USD 16,536 and USD 165,353; Form 3520 USD 100,000; exclusion USD 132,900 for 2026. The repository's figures agree.

findings.area: US exchange gain is sized in one other section only
findings.finding: Section 988 is mentioned throughout the repository. The older sections give the rule without a number. final-f6327e23 sizes the gain for 2025 renminbi at USD 6,226.68 per USD 100,000 converted at 6.6851, which agrees with this section's USD 6,227. This section adds the 2021-2024 vintages: with yearly averages of 7.075-7.189 for 2023-2025, about 5.5%-7.0% of every dollar received would be exchange gain — far more than any bank charge.

The USD 50,000-per-payment filing rule appears in a few files only. Its Article 4 — foreign individuals' payments follow the personal foreign-exchange rules — is not quoted anywhere else in the repository.

The State Council Regulations and the PBOC rules define the term differently for a foreigner who has lived in China for a year. Earlier pages note the conflict; it is still unresolved and still decides who may use the annual quota.

findings.area: Number of methods differs from page to page
findings.finding: Earlier sub-sites list 13, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22 or 24 methods; this section lists 23 because each bank with a published rate is priced separately. The lists differ in how they split the same routes, not in which routes exist.

findings.area: Two executive summaries at the repository root
findings.finding: EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md and EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY.md both exist and differ. Neither is edited here.

The IRS yearly-average table shows '0,924' for the euro in 2024 and '.73.686' for the rouble in 2021. The PBOC's English text of Decree No. 3 heads its capital-account chapter 'Under the Current Account'. Neither affects a figure used here.
